Ameliorate

uh-MEEL-yuh-rayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To ameliorate to make a bad or unsatisfactory situation better.

International aid shipments helped ameliorate the food shortage in the weeks after the earthquake.

Worked Example

New labor laws were passed to ameliorate the dangerous working conditions that factory inspectors had documented for years.

Ameliorate describes a gradual, often deliberate improvement to a bad situation -- it rarely means a problem is fixed completely.

How Strong Is It? — tweak → ameliorate → revolutionize

tweak vs. ameliorate

tweak vs. ameliorate: Tweak means to make a small adjustment or minor improvement, less significant than ameliorate.

revolutionize vs. ameliorate

revolutionize vs. ameliorate: Revolutionize means to completely transform something for the better, a far more dramatic change than simply ameliorating it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: to, toward (Latin ad-)

root — melior-

root — melior-: better (Latin melior, comparative of bonus, 'good')

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make (Latin -atus)

Put it together

Put it together: Ameliorate comes from a- ('to') + melior ('better') + -ate ('to make') -- literally 'to make better.' Latin melior doesn't survive as its own common English word, so there's no everyday root_mcq word to quiz here.

Use the root in a new word: meliorism

Use the root in a new word: meliorism: Meliorism is the belief that the world can gradually be made better through steady human effort.
